---
id: SA-0379
title: A removed name's only reader sits behind a symlink, so removed_name_readers misses it
type: bug
priority: 2
estimated_lines: 130
estimate_measured: true
touches:
  - saffron/repos/mirror.py
  - tests/test_removed_name_readers.py
forbidden:
  - DESIGN.md
  - CONTEXT.md
  - CLAUDE.md
  - README.md
  - pyproject.toml
  - uv.lock
  - .saffron/**
  - .claude/**

  - docs/**
  - harness/**
  - images/**
  - records/**
  - hooks/**
  - saffron/intake.py

  - tests/test_mirror.py
  - tests/test_task.py

  - tests/test_queued_specs.py
  - tests/test_adopt_stack_layer.py
  - tests/test_regate.py
  - tests/fixtures/**
budget_usd: 45
max_attempts: 3
max_turns: 90
acceptance:
  - claim: >-
      `removed_name_readers(mirror, sha, entries)` in `saffron/repos/mirror.py`
      finds a reader reached only through a tracked symlink. A new
      `_tracked_symlinks(mirror, sha)` lists every symlink's path in the
      tree with one `git ls-tree -r -z`, read once when `entries` is not
      empty. Each entry's own `git grep -l -z -F` still finds a candidate by
      raw blob content, matching the entry's own subject. Every path
      `_tracked_symlinks` lists also joins that entry's candidate set.
      `file_at`'s one-hop resolution then widens the search past a
      symlink's own blob, the plain target string `git grep` searches
      instead. A candidate is a reader when its `file_at` text holds the
      subject as a whole word, by `_word_pattern`, a symlink's resolved
      target or a regular file's own text alike, nested in a directory or
      not. A raw-content match that `file_at` cannot read as text at all
      stays a reader, as before. A symlink `_tracked_symlinks` alone
      offers, with no raw match and no resolved word match, is dropped
      there instead, unproven, even when `file_at` cannot read it either,
      so an escaping symlink names no reader. The entry's own path is
      still never its own reader. Pairs still come in entry order, then
      in path order, each entry's candidates sorted once the grep and
      symlink sets are merged.
    witness: tests/test_removed_name_readers.py::test_a_symlinks_resolved_content_is_checked_though_its_own_blob_never_matches
    wrong_versions:
      - "`_tracked_symlinks` left uncalled, the base build, so a reader reached only through a symlink names no pair."
      - A candidate `_tracked_symlinks` alone offers kept as a reader whenever `file_at` cannot read it, the same rule a raw-content match gets, so an escaping symlink names a pair no entry's text ever held.
      - "`git ls-tree` called without `-r`, so a symlink nested in a directory never joins a candidate set."
      - Each entry's grep hits and symlink paths sorted apart and concatenated rather than merged into one sorted set, so a symlink reader's path lands out of order against a regular reader's.
---

## Context

Backlog item `b-1c59c3` and `SA-0372` gave `removed_name_readers` its
`git grep -l -z -F` candidate search, at `saffron/repos/mirror.py:355`.
Read at head `335684ea2f112b2a3c6b035ed27a8038f148ab23`. `SA-0372`'s own
notes called a tracked symlink never a candidate. That was measured on the
host's git 2.54.0 alone. The cell image's git 2.39.5 was left unmeasured,
and no witness drove a symlink reader.

**What `git grep` does with a symlink, measured in this
session.** A symlink's blob holds its target string, not the file that
string names. A symlink's target string can still name the subject
outright. Even then, that symlink never turns into a `git grep -l -F`
match, on git 2.47.3. `git grep` reads a symlink's own blob for a match.
It reads a regular file's own blob the same way. A target string rarely
names the subject it points at.

So the gap this spec closes does not wait on an older git. `file_at`, at
`saffron/repos/mirror.py:265`, follows a symlink one hop to a regular
file, or raises `UnreadablePath`. `unresolved_consumes`, at
`saffron/repos/mirror.py:312-335`, already trusts that one-hop rule to
resolve a `path:name` entry. `removed_name_readers` trusts the same rule
for a candidate `git grep` names by raw content, at
`saffron/repos/mirror.py:371-376`. It never asks the same question of a
candidate `git grep` cannot name at all. Picture a reader reached only through a symlink, one whose own
blob never names the subject. Its `file_at` text does name the subject.
Such a reader escapes `removed_name_readers` on every git version this
repository runs, not only on one unmeasured image.

## Problem

Widen each entry's candidate set past raw `git grep` content, so a tracked
symlink whose resolved text holds the subject still names a pair. Do this
without turning an unrelated unreadable symlink into a false one.

Add `_tracked_symlinks(mirror, sha)`, beside `removed_name_readers`. Run
`git ls-tree -r -z` once over the tree-ish, and keep every path whose mode
reads `120000`. Raise `GitError` on a non-zero exit, the shape
`removed_name_readers` already raises for a `sha` the mirror lacks.

In `removed_name_readers`, call `_tracked_symlinks` once, before the
entry loop, when `entries` is not empty. Keep each entry's own `git grep`
call. Name its raw-content matches `grep_hits`, rather than folding them
straight into the candidate loop. Build each entry's candidate set as
`grep_hits` union every symlink's path, and walk it sorted. Entry order
stays outer, and path order stays the sort key, in place of git's own
listing order alone. Keep a candidate a reader when `file_at`'s text
holds the subject, by `_word_pattern`. This rule now covers a symlink's
resolved target and a regular file's own text alike, nested in a
directory or not. When `file_at` raises `UnreadablePath` or
`UnicodeDecodeError`, keep the candidate a reader only when `grep_hits`
already named it. Drop a symlink-only candidate there instead. A symlink
escaping the tree, or pointing at a submodule, then names no reader with
no evidence behind it. Keep the entry's own path excluded from its own
candidate set, symlink or not, exactly as `SA-0372` already does.

Write the witness the lone acceptance criterion names, in
`tests/test_removed_name_readers.py`, beside `SA-0372`'s own four tests.

## Out of scope

- **`run_task`'s refusal.** `saffron/task.py` already calls
  `removed_name_readers` and turns its pairs into a refusal. This spec
  edits neither call site nor refusal. A wider candidate set reaches that
  refusal through the one function alone.
- **A symlink as an entry's own path.** `SA-0372` left that case to the
  existing `candidate == path` check. This spec keeps that check as is,
  for a symlink `_tracked_symlinks` offers too.
- **A symlink the cell image's older git treats differently.** This
  session measured git 2.47.3 alone. A tracked symlink's own blob never
  names a match by raw content there. `_tracked_symlinks` reads the tree
  with `ls-tree`, not `grep`, so the fix leans on neither git version's
  grep behaviour.
- **A submodule.** `file_at` already raises `UnreadablePath` for a
  gitlink. `_tracked_symlinks` never lists one, since a gitlink's mode is
  never `120000`.

## Notes for the agent

**The one acceptance criterion is new code.** `witness` reports `skip`
for it. The mutant it names is the function this spec changes, not a
declared wrong version `revert` can restore alone.

**At base the witness fails outright.** `removed_name_readers` at
`335684ea` calls nothing named `_tracked_symlinks`. Its only candidates
come from `git grep`, so the symlink reader the witness builds names no
pair.

**Why a symlink `file_at` cannot read stays unproven.** `grep_hits` is
the only evidence a candidate's raw content ever held the subject. A
symlink `_tracked_symlinks` offers with no raw match carries no such
evidence. Keeping it on an `UnreadablePath` or a decode failure would turn
every escaping symlink in a tree into a reader. That would hold for every
entry, regardless of what either side ever named.

**The `prose` gate** counts each new comment and docstring. Write none
with an em dash, a semicolon, a contraction, the perfect tense, a filler
word, or a sentence over 25 words.

**Size.** A prototype measured 212 changed tokens in
`saffron/repos/mirror.py` with `size_gate`, against the `bug` ceiling of
1300, with 117 more under `tests/test_removed_name_readers.py`. Every
test in `tests/test_mirror.py`, `tests/test_consumes.py` and
`tests/test_task.py` passed on it, alongside every existing test in
`tests/test_removed_name_readers.py`.
